hero.description: Travel with seasoned cooks, old markets and trails of coffee, mezcal and cacao. Intimate journeys that reveal the country through what reaches the table.
hero.noteText: Every trip starts at a table, with a cook and a story no book contains.

how.title: Your journey in three steps
how.subtitle: A simple way to shape a trip of your own with the people who keep Mexican cooking alive.

steps.title: Pick your experience
steps.text: Choose a route by region, season and pace. It can be a morning at the market or a full week among haciendas.

steps.title: We tailor it with you
steps.text: A local guide joins you while we fine-tune dates, food and rhythm. We handle transport, lodging and visits with producers in their homes.

steps.title: Savour the country
steps.text: Spend full days with cooks, traders and artisans. You leave with recipes, contacts and a very personal map of Mexican flavour.

manifesto.quote: Mexico is not explained: it is savoured.
manifesto.author: The Tu Guía Viajera manifesto
manifesto.title: Cooking that begins at the hearth
manifesto.body1: We want to show the Mexico cooked over a hearth, not plated on a tasting menu. We work with traditional cooks, producers and artisans in their own kitchens and markets.
manifesto.body2: We aim for every route to leave more value in the community than footprint on the destination. Eating here is also a way to understand the country; tasting it at its source is the most honest way to know it.

featured.title: Routes with Flavour
featured.subtitle: Journeys shaped hand in hand with the people who keep Mexican cooking alive.

impact.title: Every route pays directly to the people who make it possible.
impact.body: We are not middlemen of flavour. We design every experience with local cooks, producers and guides, and we make sure the value stays in their territory.
impact.label1: of each route’s value stays in the community
impact.label2: states of Mexico on our map

story.title: The Mexico that simmers over the fire
story.body1: Our idea began with a simple observation: the best Mexico is cooked far from tasting menus. So we walk alongside traditional cooks, producers and artisans, inside their kitchens and markets.
story.body2: Every trip tries to leave more money in the community than marks on the destination. Eating in Mexico is a history lesson too; doing it at its source is the most sincere way to learn it.

faq.title: What people usually ask
faq.subtitle: Bookings, payment, languages and dietary needs: what you need before sitting at the table.

items.q: How do I book a route?
items.a: Pick it from the catalogue, write to us from the contact page or book on the experience page. Within 24 hours we confirm availability and send you the itinerary and a payment link.

items.q: What is covered by the price?
items.a: Each experience lists what it includes; as a rule this covers a local guide, the meals and tastings mentioned, entry to homes, workshops and markets, internal transport and taxes. Prices are always shown in MXN with VAT included. Flights and lodging are quoted separately except on multi-day routes.

items.q: Do you arrange private groups or events?
items.a: We do. We create private journeys for families, couples, friends and company teams. Tell us your idea and we will propose a plan with dates and group sizes to match.

items.q: How do payment and cancellations work?
items.a: We accept Visa, Mastercard and bank transfer. Cancel 30 or more days ahead for a full refund; between 30 and 14 days you get 50%; under 14 days there is no refund unless illness can be proven.

items.q: Are routes offered in other languages?
items.a: Routes usually run in Spanish. For international groups we have bilingual Spanish-English guides; just mention it when booking.

items.q: Can you adapt to dietary restrictions?
items.a: Yes. We adjust the experience for vegetarians, vegans, coeliacs, dairy-free guests and other needs. Let us know when booking so we can warn the cooks in advance.
